experiences.name: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, just a short walk from Lagos town center. Praia Dona Ana features dramatic golden limestone cliffs, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and soft sand. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, explore the sea caves by foot at low tide, and enjoy fresh seafood at the beachside restaurant.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé and Quinta dos Vales reds, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. Learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve wine region from a knowledgeable sommelier.

experiences.name: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic sea caves and golden rock arches of Ponta da Piedade on a guided kayak tour departing from Lagos marina. Snorkel in hidden grottos and lagoons teeming with marine life, and witness breathtaking coastal scenery accessible only by water. A perfect blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting
experiences.description: Take a half-day excursion to one of the Algarve's premier wineries, Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of five award-winning wines including their signature Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculptures and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Stroll along the vast 4km stretch of Meia Praia, a wide sandy beach just east of Lagos, during the golden hour for spectacular Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, dine at a local beachside restaurant serving freshly grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and local Algarve wines, combining the best of beach culture and regional cuisine.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24h petrol station near the bus terminal or a kebab shop near Lagos center (~€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro–Lagos bus ticket online at rede-expressos.pt to save time. The hostel is a short walk or cheap taxi (~€5) from Lagos bus station. Keep energy for tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy the hostel's communal area. Walk to the historic old town of Lagos — explore the 16th-century city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the free Igreja de Santo António exterior and the nearby Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long golden beach just east of Lagos (15-min walk or free bike from hostel if available). Swim, relax, and soak up the September sun. The crowds thin out in mid-September making it ideal. Explore the rock formations at Ponta da Piedade on foot (30-min walk from town) — stunning golden cliffs and sea caves, completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of Rua 25 de Abril, Lagos's main bar street. Grab a cheap beer or glass of local wine at one of the outdoor terraces.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota or any local café near the hostel — coffee + pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Grab a prego (steak sandwich) or bifana at a local tasca near the market (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or Restaurante Adega da Marina — try grilled sardines or bacalhau (cod) with house wine (~€10-13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Algarve is warm (24-28°C) with minimal rain — perfect beach weather. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (Eva Bus line, ~€2.50) or rent a bicycle (~€10/day from Lagos bike shops) to Praia da Luz, a quieter village beach 6km west of Lagos. Swim and explore the dramatic black rock cliffs framing the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue west by bus or bike to Burgau, a tiny whitewashed fishing village with a small beach. Walk the coastal trail between Burgau and Luz for stunning cliff views (free, ~45 min one way). Return to Lagos by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) area for a local feel. Join a free walking tour of Lagos old town (tip-based, ~€5 tip recommended) — check hostel noticeboard for schedules.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen self-catering — buy bread, cheese, and fruit from the local Pingo Doce supermarket (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Luz — fresh grilled fish sandwich and a beer (~€7-9)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos old town — hearty Portuguese home cooking, daily specials ~€8-10

day_by_day.notes: Renting a bike is a great budget option for exploring the western Algarve coast. The coastal path between Burgau and Luz is one of the most scenic short hikes in the region.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — take the Eva Bus from Lagos bus station (~€4.50 each way, ~1 hour). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe with breathtaking Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente (3km from Sagres or take a taxi ~€5), the most southwestern point of continental Europe. The lighthouse and cliffs are spectacular and free to visit. Watch surfers at Praia do Tonel near Sagres — one of the best surf beaches in Portugal.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Relax at the hostel and mingle with fellow travelers. Head out for drinks on Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Café in Sagres village — coffee and toast (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres — fresh tuna steak or grilled fish with salad (~€9-12)
meals.dinner: Nah Nah Bah burger bar in Lagos — great burgers and craft beer, budget-friendly (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is windier and cooler than Lagos — bring a light jacket. The last bus back to Lagos is usually around 19:00-19:30, so check the timetable at the Lagos bus station before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most iconic beaches, a 20-min walk from the hostel. Arrive early to claim a good spot. The golden rock arches and turquoise water are stunning. Snorkel around the rock formations (bring your own snorkel or rent ~€5).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the cliff-top trail from Praia Dona Ana to Ponta da Piedade and back (~2 hours round trip, free). The views of the sea stacks and grottos are world-class. Optionally, book a kayak or boat cave tour from the beach (~€15-20 — one of the best budget splurges in the Algarve).
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in Lagos — the town comes alive. Enjoy a sunset drink at Bon Vivant rooftop bar. Explore the nightlife on Rua 25 de Abril. Many bars offer happy hour deals (2-for-1 drinks) from 18:00-20:00.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria near the hostel — galão (milky coffee) + croissant (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from Pingo Doce supermarket — bread, local cheese, olives, fruit (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco — traditional Algarvian cuisine, try cataplana (seafood stew) shared between two (~€12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day in Lagos. Book the kayak/boat tour in advance at the beach kiosk or through the hostel. The cliff walk is free and arguably better than the paid boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a morning bus or taxi (~€15) to Quinta da Penina or Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar/Lagoa (30 min east of Lagos). Many Algarve quintas offer free or low-cost tastings (~€5-10) of local Algarve wines including Negra Mole and Arinto varieties. Book ahead by phone or email.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Silves — take a bus from Lagoa (~€2.50). Visit the stunning red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Wander the charming medieval town and the Gothic cathedral (free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus (~€3.50 from Silves). Relax at the hostel. Cook a simple dinner in the hostel kitchen using local ingredients from the market.

meals.breakfast: Hostel self-catering — yogurt, fruit, and bread (~€2)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — great views of the castle, sandwiches and salads (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hostel meal — pasta with local chorizo and vegetables (~€3-4 per person from supermarket)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales (quintadosvales.eu) is one of the most visitor-friendly wineries in the Algarve and offers affordable tastings. Call ahead to confirm Sunday opening hours. Silves is a highlight of the Algarve interior — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the Eva Bus from Lagos (~€3, 30 min). Praia da Rocha is a wide, dramatic beach with impressive rock formations. Arrive early to explore before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the cliff-top promenade at Praia da Rocha. Visit the small Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (free entry) overlooking the Arade River estuary. Take a short ferry across the river to Ferragudo (~€1.50), a picturesque fishing village with a lovely beach and castle views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão and catch the bus back to Lagos. Portimão is famous for its sardine grilling — try the waterfront restaurants near the old fish market for the freshest sardines in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Café in Portimão near the bus station — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Rocha — grilled chicken piri-piri wrap (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão waterfront — grilled sardines with bread and salad, house wine (~€10-12) before catching the last bus back

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most underrated villages in the Algarve — very photogenic and far less touristy than Portimão. The ferry runs frequently and costs about €1.50 each way.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning in Lagos. Visit the Farmers' Market at Mercado Municipal de Lagos (open until ~13:00) — buy local honey, almonds, figs, and cheese. Great for budget snacks and picnic supplies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or SUP board from the beach (~€10-15/hour) at Meia Praia. Paddle along the coastline for a different perspective of the Lagos cliffs. Alternatively, take a free self-guided walk along the Via Algarviana coastal path section near Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free Fado music performance — check with the hostel or local tourism office for free or low-cost Fado nights at local restaurants or cultural centers. Enjoy a glass of local Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh fruit, local bread, and a coffee from a market stall (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Meia Praia using market purchases (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos — traditional Portuguese dishes, excellent value menu do dia (~€9-11)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos Municipal Market is a great place to interact with locals and buy authentic regional products at low prices. Fado nights are sometimes hosted at local restaurants for free — ask at the hostel reception.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting excursion — visit Adega Cooperativa do Algarve or Quinta do Barranco Longo near Lagoa/Carvoeiro area (bus to Lagoa ~€3, then taxi ~€8). These cooperatives offer very affordable tastings and cellar tours (~€5-8). Buy a bottle of local wine to enjoy later.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Carvoeiro village on the way back — a charming small resort town with a pretty beach in a cove. Walk the Algar Seco boardwalk (free) — dramatic rock formations and sea caves carved by the Atlantic. Return to Lagos by bus via Lagoa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Lagos city walls viewpoint. Cook dinner at the hostel or grab takeaway. Share wine purchased from the winery with fellow hostel guests.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen — toast, local jam, and coffee (~€1-2)
meals.lunch: Snack bar in Carvoeiro — prego sandwich and local beer (~€7-8)
meals.dinner: Takeaway from Frango Assado (rotisserie chicken) near Lagos center — half chicken, fries, and salad (~€6-8)

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco in Carvoeiro is completely free and one of the most dramatic coastal landscapes in the Algarve. The Lagoa cooperative wines are excellent value — a good bottle costs €4-7 direct from the producer.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve coast — take a bus toward Vila do Bispo (~€3.50). Walk or hike a section of the Rota Vicentina / Fishermen's Trail (Trilho dos Pescadores), one of Europe's most beautiful coastal walking routes. The section between Praia do Castelejo and Praia da Cordoama is spectacular (free, ~2 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at Praia do Castelejo — a wild, unspoiled Atlantic beach backed by cliffs. Far fewer tourists than Lagos beaches. Return to Lagos by bus in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate the halfway point of the trip. Explore the Lagos nightlife scene — the hostel bar is a great place to meet other travelers.

meals.breakfast: Café in Vila do Bispo — coffee and local pastry (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the supermarket for the hike (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — splurge slightly on a cataplana or fresh grilled sea bass (~€14-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Fishermen's Trail is one of Portugal's great hidden gems. Wear sturdy shoes and bring plenty of water. Praia do Castelejo can have strong Atlantic swells — check conditions before swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tavira — take the train from Lagos (change at Faro, total ~2.5 hours, ~€8-10 each way). Tavira is considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins (free), and the charming whitewashed streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira (~€1.50 each way) — a barrier island beach that is one of the finest in the Algarve. The beach is wide, pristine, and backed by dunes. Swim and relax before catching the ferry back.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tavira's evening atmosphere — the town is lively on Friday nights. Catch the train back to Lagos (last train check timetable carefully). Arrive back at the hostel by 22:00-23:00.

meals.breakfast: Café near Lagos train station — coffee and toast (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Ilha de Tavira — fresh grilled fish and salad (~€10-12)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Corvo in Tavira — excellent local food, petiscos (Portuguese tapas) style (~€10-13) before catching the train

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a full-day trip from Lagos. Check the CP (Comboios de Portugal) train timetable at cp.pt before going. The last train from Tavira toward Lagos is usually around 20:00-21:00 — don't miss it!

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — revisit your favorite Lagos beach (Praia Dona Ana or Meia Praia recommended). Take a final cliff walk along Ponta da Piedade. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy the last full day of Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse the Lagos Saturday market and artisan shops for budget souvenirs — local almonds, carob products, ceramic tiles, and cork items make great gifts. Visit the Lagos Zoo if traveling with family (~€13 entry) or skip for free beach time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos. Splurge slightly on a memorable final meal. Afterward, enjoy a final sunset drink at a rooftop bar. Pack bags for departure tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Café Atlântico near the hostel — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, bread, and coffee (~€5-6)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — grilled sardines, salad, and a cold Super Bock beer (~€9-11)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco — final splurge on cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) with local wine (~€16-18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Buy local products like Algarve honey, medronho (arbutus berry spirit), and almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo) as souvenirs — they're affordable and authentically Algarvian. Medronho is available at most supermarkets for ~€5-8.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (standard checkout 10:00-11:00 — confirm with hostel). Store luggage at the hostel if your bus/flight is later. Take a final morning walk through Lagos old town — visit the Igreja de Santa Maria and the waterfront one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Lagos bus station to Faro Airport (~€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time before your departure flight. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Portuguese wine or port.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the Algarve's beaches, wines, and culture!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagos café — a proper Portuguese farewell (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Light snack at Faro Airport or pack leftovers from the hostel kitchen (~€5-8 at airport)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate: Accommodation at Boutique Taghostel (hostel dorm ~€20-30/night x 12 nights = ~€240-360). Food ~€20-25/day = ~€260-325. Transport ~€80-100. Activities/entrance fees ~€50-70. Wine tastings ~€30-40. Total estimated budget: ~€660-895 for 13 days — very achievable for a budget-conscious traveler in the Algarve!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or a pre-booked taxi (~45 min, ~€50) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour convenience store or the hostel's common area if snacks are available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a convenience store near the hostel or airport grab-and-go options at Faro

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid waiting at night. Confirm check-in arrangements with Taghostel as arrival is late. Pack light for easy movement upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Take a gentle orientation walk through Lagos old town – explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia Dona Ana Beach (a 15-minute walk from the hostel). Spend the afternoon relaxing on one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, framed by golden limestone cliffs. Swim, sunbathe, and soak in the scenery. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for comfort (~€10).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Stroll along the marina and watch the sunset over the water. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel – try a pastel de nata and galão coffee (~€5)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia Dona Ana – grilled fish sandwich or salad (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant near Praia Dona Ana or Adega da Marina in Lagos town – grilled sea bass or cataplana (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm and sunny in the Algarve – perfect beach weather. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Praia Dona Ana is a short, easy walk from the hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour (book in advance, departs from Lagos marina or Ponta da Piedade, ~10 min from hostel). Paddle through iconic sea caves, golden rock arches, and hidden grottos. The tour typically runs 2.5–3 hours (~€35–45 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, dry off and head to Praia do Camilo, a secluded beach near Ponta da Piedade accessible via wooden stairs. Relax and enjoy the dramatic cliff scenery. Alternatively, explore the clifftop walking trail between Ponta da Piedade and Lagos for stunning panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Head back into Lagos for the evening. Browse the local shops and artisan stalls near Rua 25 de Abril. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Meia Lua Café or Pastelaria Mota in Lagos – toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch from a local deli or supermarket (Pingo Doce nearby) – cheese, bread, local olives, and fruit (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Lagos – traditional Portuguese petiscos (tapas-style sharing plates) and local wine (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak tour at least 1–2 days in advance, especially in September. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes and bring a change of clothes. The snorkeling portion reveals colorful marine life in crystal-clear waters.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi to Sagres (40 min west of Lagos, ~€5 by bus). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept promontory at the southwestern tip of Europe. Explore the historic compass rose and enjoy breathtaking Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente (5 km from Sagres or take a taxi), the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Watch the waves crash against the cliffs and visit the lighthouse. Return to Sagres village for a relaxed afternoon exploring the local surf culture and beaches like Praia do Martinhal.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus or taxi. Enjoy a quiet evening in the hostel common area meeting fellow travelers, or take a sunset walk along the Lagos waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a quick café stop in Lagos before departure (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: A Sagres – local restaurant in Sagres village serving fresh grilled fish and seafood (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco in Lagos – cozy Portuguese restaurant with daily specials and local wine (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. The last bus back to Lagos typically departs around 18:30–19:00; check the Eva Transportes schedule. Alternatively, rent a car for the day for more flexibility (~€30–40).

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy the Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center. Sample regional wines from the Alentejo and Algarve appellations paired with local cheeses, cured meats, and artisan bread. The guided session typically runs 1.5–2 hours (~€30–40 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk off the tasting with a visit to the Mercado de Lagos (Lagos Municipal Market) – browse fresh produce, local honey, almonds, and handmade crafts. Then visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church with gilded woodwork, and the adjacent Museu Municipal de Lagos (~€3 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening in Lagos. Visit a wine bar for a glass of local Algarve wine before dinner, continuing the wine theme of the day.

meals.breakfast: Café Correia in Lagos – a local favorite for fresh pastries and coffee (~€5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch included or supplemented during the wine tasting, or grab a bifana (pork sandwich) from a local tasca (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: No Pátio Restaurant in Lagos – Mediterranean-Portuguese fusion with an excellent wine list (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the wine tasting experience in advance as Saturday sessions fill up quickly. September is harvest season in Portugal, making this an especially authentic time to taste local wines. Ask the sommelier about visiting local quintas (wine estates) for further exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter from a Lagos rental shop (~€15–25/day) and cycle along the coastal path toward Meia Praia, a long, sweeping sandy beach east of Lagos. Enjoy the morning light on the water and take a refreshing swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cycling or take a short taxi to Alvor, a charming fishing village with a beautiful estuary and boardwalk. Walk the wooden boardwalk through the Ria de Alvor nature reserve, spotting birds and enjoying the peaceful lagoon scenery. Explore Alvor's whitewashed old town and castle ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed Sunday evening with a drink at a rooftop bar or terrace overlooking the town.

meals.breakfast: Padaria Pastelaria Mota in Lagos – fresh bread, cheese, and coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso in Alvor – a beloved local spot for grilled fish and seafood rice (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – traditional Algarvian cuisine including cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is accessible by a short ferry from Lagos marina (€1.50 each way) or by bicycle along the road. Alvor is approximately 10 km east of Lagos. Sunday can be quieter in villages – a perfect day for a slower pace.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (30 min by train from Lagos, ~€3.50). Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Explore the castle walls and enjoy panoramic views over the surrounding orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Silves old town, visit the Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Silves), and browse the local shops. Stop at a local quinta or wine shop in Silves to taste Algarve wines – the region around Silves is known for its vineyards. Return to Lagos by train in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hostel or take an evening stroll along the Lagos waterfront. Enjoy a casual dinner at a local tasca.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Lagos train station café or hostel (~€5)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves – a charming restaurant within the castle grounds serving local dishes (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Tasca da Praça in Lagos – a small, authentic Portuguese restaurant with daily specials and house wine (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos–Silves train journey is scenic and affordable. Trains run roughly every 1–2 hours. Silves is also famous for its annual Medieval Fair (usually August), but September still offers a lively atmosphere. Wear comfortable shoes for the castle cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia Dona Ana for a second beach day, this time exploring the surrounding coves and rock formations more actively. Hire a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) or join a guided cliff walk along the coastline between Lagos and Ponta da Piedade (~€15–20 for SUP rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia do Porto de Mós, a quieter beach slightly further from Lagos (20-min walk or short taxi). Enjoy the calmer atmosphere, clear waters, and dramatic cliff backdrop. Bring a book and fully unwind.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Lagos for a wine-focused evening. Visit a local wine bar for a curated tasting of Alentejo and Algarve wines by the glass, paired with local charcuterie.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha in Lagos – yogurt, granola, and fresh juice (~€7–9)
meals.lunch: Beach kiosk at Praia do Porto de Mós – grilled sardines, salad, and local beer (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Vinha Bar in Lagos – wine bar with an excellent selection of Portuguese wines and small plates (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September waters in the Algarve are warm (around 22–24°C) – ideal for swimming and water sports. Porto de Mós beach has limited facilities compared to Dona Ana, so bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Portimão and Ferragudo (30 min east by bus or taxi). Start with a visit to the Museu de Portimão, an award-winning museum housed in a former sardine canning factory – fascinating insight into the region's fishing heritage (~€3 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Arade River by ferry to the picturesque village of Ferragudo. Explore the castle, whitewashed houses, and fishing harbor. Relax on Praia Grande de Ferragudo, a beautiful sandy beach with views back toward Portimão. Return to Lagos by bus in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening in Lagos. Visit the weekly local market if running, or browse artisan shops for souvenirs – local almonds, carob products, and Algarvian ceramics make great gifts.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café in Lagos (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo – renowned for fresh seafood and river views (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: A Forja in Lagos – a long-standing local favorite for grilled meats and fish with house wine (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Portimão–Ferragudo ferry is a fun and cheap way to cross the river (~€1). Ferragudo is one of the Algarve's most authentic and photogenic villages – bring your camera. Buses between Lagos and Portimão run frequently throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided jeep safari or off-road tour into the Algarve hinterland (Costa Vicentina Natural Park or the Serra de Monchique foothills). These tours depart from Lagos and explore cork oak forests, traditional villages, and scenic viewpoints (~€45–60 per person, half-day option available).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos and spend the afternoon at leisure. Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) – the only remaining slave market building in Europe, with a sobering and important historical exhibition (~€3 entry). Stroll through the Jardim da Constituição for a peaceful rest.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dinner experience to mark the midpoint of the trip. Choose a restaurant with a good wine list and enjoy a multi-course Portuguese meal.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota in Lagos – croissant, cheese toast, and coffee (~€6)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the jeep safari tour, or a quick stop at a local village café during the tour
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira in Lagos – elegant but mid-range Portuguese cuisine with regional wines (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the jeep safari in advance. Half-day morning tours are ideal for combining with afternoon activities. The Slave Market Museum is small but deeply significant – allow 45–60 minutes for a thoughtful visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Monchique, a mountain spa town in the Serra de Monchique (1 hour by bus from Portimão, or taxi from Lagos ~€40 one way). Hike to the summit of Fóia, the highest point in the Algarve (902m), for sweeping views over the coast and countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Monchique town – visit the ruined Franciscan convent, browse local shops selling medronho (arbutus berry brandy) and honey, and relax in the peaceful mountain atmosphere. Stop at Caldas de Monchique, a charming spa village in a wooded valley, for a stroll and a taste of the famous mineral water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a final Friday evening in the lively town center – Lagos has a vibrant but relaxed nightlife scene with wine bars and live music venues.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or Lagos café before departure (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique – hearty mountain cuisine including pork with clams (carne de porco à alentejana) and local wine (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Lagos – casual seafood restaurant with cold beer and fresh shellfish (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The bus from Lagos to Portimão then Portimão to Monchique is the budget option but takes 1.5–2 hours total. A shared taxi or rental car is more convenient. Bring a light layer – Monchique is noticeably cooler than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final full morning at your favorite beach – return to Praia Dona Ana or try Praia da Luz (20 min west of Lagos by bus), a quieter resort beach with a dramatic black rock formation. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy the last full beach day of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon of exploration. Revisit any spots you loved, pick up last-minute souvenirs, and stop at a local wine shop (like Garrafeira do Mercado) to purchase bottles of Algarve or Alentejo wine to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the final evening with a special farewell dinner. Choose a restaurant that best represents your Algarve experience – fresh seafood, local wine, and the warm Portuguese hospitality that defines the region.

meals.breakfast: Café Correia in Lagos – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, and coffee (~€7–9)
meals.lunch: Beach bar at Praia da Luz or a picnic with local market purchases (~€10–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo (cliff-top restaurant near Praia Dona Ana) – fresh seafood with stunning ocean views, a memorable farewell meal (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner at O Camilo in advance – it's popular and has limited seating. The cliff-top setting at sunset is spectacular. Visit the wine shop early in the afternoon as some close by 18:00 on Saturdays.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast in Lagos. Take one last walk through the old town, along the city walls, and down to the marina to say goodbye to the Algarve. Pack and check out of Boutique Taghostel (standard checkout is 11:00 – confirm with the hostel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either relax at a café in Lagos or head to Faro Airport. The transfer from Lagos to Faro Airport takes approximately 45–60 minutes by taxi (~€50) or 1.5–2 hours by bus (Eva Transportes, ~€6). Allow ample time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, culture, and the golden light of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagos café – a perfect last taste of Portugal (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Lagos before departure, or at Faro Airport (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Store luggage at the hostel after checkout if your transfer isn't until the afternoon. Confirm your taxi or transfer booking the night before. Faro Airport has limited dining options – eat well in Lagos before heading to the airport. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, just a short walk from Lagos town center. Praia Dona Ana features dramatic golden limestone cliffs, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and soft sand. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, explore the sea caves by foot at low tide, and enjoy fresh seafood at the beachside restaurant.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé and Quinta dos Vales reds, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. Learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve wine region from a knowledgeable sommelier.

experiences.name: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic sea caves and golden rock arches of Ponta da Piedade on a guided kayak tour departing from Lagos marina. Snorkel in hidden grottos and lagoons teeming with marine life, and witness breathtaking coastal scenery accessible only by water. A perfect blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting
experiences.description: Take a half-day excursion to one of the Algarve's premier wineries, Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of five award-winning wines including their signature Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculptures and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Stroll along the vast 4km stretch of Meia Praia, a wide sandy beach just east of Lagos, during the golden hour for spectacular Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, dine at a local beachside restaurant serving freshly grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and local Algarve wines, combining the best of beach culture and regional cuisine.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour drive). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine at the hotel's lounge or terrace.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board with a glass of Alentejo red wine at the hotel lounge upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private chauffeur transfer from Faro Airport to Lagos for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm with hotel for a late check-in and request a welcome amenity. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a gourmet breakfast at the hotel. Take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos' historic old town – explore the 16th-century city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day: Head to one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches, just a short walk from the hotel. Settle into a premium sun lounger, swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters framed by dramatic golden limestone cliffs, and soak in the stunning scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Enjoy a sunset cocktail on the hotel terrace, then head to dinner at a top Lagos restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Boutique Taghostel – fresh pastries, local cheeses, cured meats, fruit, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach-side café near Praia Dona Ana – grilled sea bass, fresh salads, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at No Pátio (Lagos) – a refined Portuguese restaurant known for its seasonal tasting menus and excellent local wine list

day_by_day.notes: Praia Dona Ana is a short walk or quick taxi from the hotel. Arrive early afternoon to secure the best spot. September weather is typically warm and sunny with fewer crowds than peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience: Join a guided morning wine tasting session at a curated Lagos wine bar near the historic center. Sample regional Algarve and Alentejo wines paired with artisan local cheeses, cured meats, and traditional accompaniments, guided by a knowledgeable sommelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos' cultural highlights: visit the Igreja de Santo António (a stunning baroque church), the Municipal Museum, and browse the artisan boutiques and galleries in the old town. Pick up premium local products – olive oils, wines, and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along the Lagos marina promenade. Enjoy a pre-dinner aperitivo at a waterfront bar before a sophisticated seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Tapas-style lunch at a wine bar following the tasting – included charcuterie boards and small plates
meals.dinner: Dinner at Casinha do Petisco (Lagos) – celebrated for its creative takes on traditional Algarvian seafood dishes in an intimate setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the wine tasting experience in advance to secure a private or small-group session for a more exclusive experience. The historic center is entirely walkable from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour: Embark on a guided kayak and snorkel adventure through the world-famous sea caves, golden rock arches, and hidden grottos of Ponta da Piedade. Paddle through emerald waters and discover secluded beaches accessible only by sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel, shower, and relax. Spend the afternoon at leisure – enjoy the hotel's amenities, read on the terrace, or book an in-room massage or spa treatment for post-kayak recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk: Take a private taxi to Meia Praia, the vast 4km sandy beach east of Lagos. Stroll along the shoreline at golden hour, watching the sun dip toward the Atlantic. Transition seamlessly into a premium seafood dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a cliffside restaurant near Ponta da Piedade – grilled octopus, prawns, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner: Dine at a top beachfront restaurant at Meia Praia – whole grilled fish, cataplana (traditional Algarvian seafood stew), and local wines

day_by_day.notes: The kayak tour typically departs in the morning when seas are calmest. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring a change of clothes. Book the tour in advance. Arrange a taxi or private driver for the Meia Praia evening excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting: Depart by private car to Quinta dos Vales, one of the Algarve's premier wineries near Estômbar (~30 min from Lagos). Enjoy a guided half-day tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a premium tasting of their award-winning reds, whites, and rosés, paired with local delicacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Silves region – visit the magnificent Moorish Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved medieval fortresses in Portugal, and wander through the charming town below.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by private transfer. Relax at the hotel before heading out for a refined dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Wine-paired lunch at Quinta dos Vales – included in the vineyard experience, featuring local cheeses, charcuterie, and seasonal dishes
meals.dinner: Dinner at Adega da Marina (Lagos) – a beloved local institution serving traditional Algarvian cuisine with an extensive regional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for the full day to Quinta dos Vales and Silves – this allows flexibility and ensures a safe return after wine tasting. Book the vineyard tour in advance, requesting a private tasting for the most exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at leisure. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time exploring the Lagos Saturday market (if still running) or the local artisan shops. Pick up premium souvenirs – local honey, fig products, and handcrafted ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Praia Dona Ana or explore nearby Praia do Camilo – a smaller, more secluded gem accessible via a wooden staircase through the cliffs. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery in a more intimate setting.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Atlantic. Enjoy a leisurely fine dining dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the hotel – treat yourself to the full spread
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch on the beach – arrange with the hotel to prepare a premium hamper with local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, fruit, and a bottle of chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bon Vivant Restaurant & Lounge (Lagos) – sophisticated international and Portuguese cuisine with an excellent cocktail bar and wine list

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo is a short walk from Praia Dona Ana and offers a more secluded experience. The wooden staircase descent is easy but wear appropriate footwear. Ask the hotel to prepare a luxury beach hamper the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente: Depart by private car to Sagres (~30 min west of Lagos). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a historic fortress perched on a windswept promontory. Then drive to Cabo de São Vicente – the southwesternmost point of continental Europe – for breathtaking Atlantic panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the wild, unspoiled beaches of the Sagres area: Praia do Beliche (a hidden gem tucked beneath the cliffs) or Praia da Mareta. Enjoy the raw, rugged beauty of the Costa Vicentina, a protected natural park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening with dinner at a local favourite.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Sagres seafood restaurant – fresh tuna, barnacles (percebes), and local fish with cold Sagres beer or white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at O Camilo Restaurant (Lagos) – perched above the cliffs near Praia do Camilo, offering spectacular views and exceptional fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September – bring a light layer. The drive along the coast is scenic and worth taking slowly. A private driver is recommended for the full day to maximize flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Wellness morning: Book a luxury spa treatment at a premium Lagos spa or arrange an in-hotel massage. Follow with a yoga or meditation session on the hotel terrace or a nearby clifftop spot overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Algarve's interior: Take a private guided tour to the traditional village of Alte, known as the 'prettiest village in the Algarve.' Wander its whitewashed streets, visit the historic church, and discover the natural spring and waterfall.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a sophisticated wine-focused dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Light, healthy breakfast at the hotel – fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a local tasca in Alte – homestyle Algarvian dishes like carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) and local bread
meals.dinner: Return to the Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting venue or a Lagos wine bar for a curated dinner pairing – premium wines matched with a seasonal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Alte is approximately 45 minutes from Lagos by private car. The village is best explored on foot. September is ideal – warm but not overwhelmingly hot for walking. Book spa treatments in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Boat trip along the Algarve coast: Book a private luxury yacht or catamaran charter departing from Lagos Marina. Sail along the stunning coastline, visiting hidden sea caves, secluded beaches, and the iconic rock formations between Lagos and Portimão.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat trip – anchor at a secluded cove for swimming and snorkeling in crystal-clear waters. Enjoy a champagne and canapé spread on deck as you cruise back toward Lagos in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the hotel terrace or a clifftop viewpoint. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at one of Lagos' finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on the yacht – arranged by the charter company or hotel: fresh seafood, premium charcuterie, local cheeses, fruit, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vitor's Restaurant (Lagos) – one of the Algarve's most acclaimed fine dining establishments, known for its creative Portuguese cuisine and exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book a private yacht or catamaran charter well in advance – September is still popular. Request a fully crewed private charter for the most exclusive experience. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the sea breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha: Take a private car to Portimão (~15 min from Lagos). Visit the Museu de Portimão, an award-winning museum housed in a former sardine canning factory, offering fascinating insights into the region's maritime and industrial heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha – one of the Algarve's most famous beaches, with its wide golden sands and dramatic rock formations. Relax on a premium sun lounger, swim, and enjoy the vibrant beach atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's waterfront dining scene before returning to Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Portimão waterfront restaurant – grilled sardines (a regional specialty), fresh bread, and local salads
meals.dinner: Dinner at Taberna da Maré (Portimão) – a celebrated seafood restaurant on the waterfront, known for its exceptional cataplana and fresh fish, before returning to Lagos

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is easily reached by private car or even by river ferry from Lagos Marina for a scenic approach. The Museu de Portimão is free on Sunday afternoons. Praia da Rocha has premium beach clubs with sun lounger service.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Quinta dos Vales or explore a different Algarve winery: Visit Adega do Cantor (near Guia, ~45 min from Lagos) – the winery associated with Sir Cliff Richard, producing acclaimed Algarve wines. Enjoy a private tour and tasting of their premium labels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the charming town of Carvoeiro on the return journey – explore the picturesque fishing village, walk the clifftop boardwalk at Algar Seco (a stunning natural rock formation), and enjoy the relaxed coastal atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a final evening of leisure – perhaps a cocktail masterclass at a Lagos bar or a private mixology session arranged through the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Wine-paired lunch at the winery or a nearby restaurant in Guia – regional dishes with estate wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at A Forja (Lagos) – a long-standing Lagos favourite known for its generous portions of traditional Portuguese cuisine and warm, convivial atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor requires advance booking for tours and tastings. Algar Seco in Carvoeiro is a short walk from the village center and is particularly beautiful in the late afternoon light. Arrange a private driver for the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning: Return to your favourite beach – whether Praia Dona Ana, Praia do Camilo, or Meia Praia – for one last luxurious morning by the sea. Swim, relax, and savour the Algarve's stunning coastal beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a leisurely afternoon of last-minute shopping and exploration. Visit the Mercado de Lagos (local market) for premium local products to take home – wines, olive oils, jams, and ceramics. Enjoy a final stroll through the historic old town.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of the trip – a memorable final evening in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch – fresh seafood, salads, and chilled local wine at a beachside restaurant
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Vitor's Restaurant or No Pátio (Lagos) – opt for the full tasting menu with wine pairing for a truly memorable final evening

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-perishable local products carefully for the journey home. Confirm checkout time and arrange luggage storage at the hotel if needed. Book the farewell dinner well in advance to secure the best table.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos: Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Take a final walk along the Lagos waterfront or up to the clifftop viewpoint above Praia Dona Ana for one last panoramic view of the Algarve coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Boutique Taghostel. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final coffee and pastel de nata at a Lagos café before your private luxury transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry home memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve – golden beaches, world-class wines, dramatic sea caves, and the warmth of Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the hotel – savour every bite
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a Lagos café or restaurant near the hotel before transfer – petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and a final glass of local wine
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private airport transfer to Faro at least 3 hours before your flight departure. Confirm all bookings and settle any outstanding hotel charges the evening before. Request a late checkout if your flight allows – the hotel may accommodate for a premium fee.
